verdict.rationale: A CPU is not normally operated by commands. However, Intel's Core Ultra marketing says Intel-enabled AI PCs support full Copilot+ integration and that users can 'use voice commands to get answers, edit content.' That puts natural-language operation into the product's own pitch, so the axis applies. The capability actually comes from Microsoft's Copilot+ on the host PC, not the processor, and evidence is limited to one marketing line. Missing for 10: any first-party natural-language interface to the processor itself, documentation of how voice/NL commands work on this chip, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
